claims.sentence: The plain-language guidance published through Digital.gov states the first rule of plain language.
claims.quote: The first rule of plain language is: write for your audience.

claims.sentence: The W3C WAI writing tips say to use simple language and formatting as appropriate for the context.
claims.locator: Tip: Keep content clear and concise
claims.quote: Use simple language and formatting, as appropriate for the context.

claims.sentence: The FTC compliance guide says the law makes no exception for business-to-business email.
claims.quote: The law makes no exception for business-to-business email.

claims.sentence: The FTC guide says a seller that pays or benefits others for traffic or referrals is likely to have CAN-SPAM obligations.
claims.locator: Compliance guide, responsibility for referral and traffic payments
claims.quote: the seller is likely to have compliance obligations under the CAN-SPAM Act.

claims.sentence: The FTC influencer guidance says to disclose financial, employment, personal or family relationships with a brand.
claims.quote: Disclose when you have any financial, employment, personal, or family relationship with a brand.

claims.sentence: Google's guide says some changes take effect in hours and others could take months.
claims.locator: SEO starter guide, how long changes take
claims.quote: Some changes might take effect in a few hours, others could take several months.

claims.sentence: The law makes no exception for business-to-business email.
claims.quote: The law makes no exception for business-to-business email.

claims.sentence: The guide defines a commercial message by its primary purpose.
claims.quote: any electronic mail message the primary purpose of which is the commercial advertisement or promotion

claims.sentence: Header information must not be false or misleading.
claims.quote: Don't use false or misleading header information.

claims.sentence: The statute refers to materially false or misleading header information.
claims.quote: header information that is materially false or materially misleading

claims.sentence: Subject lines must not be deceptive.
claims.quote: Don't use deceptive subject lines.

claims.sentence: The statute refers to a subject heading likely to mislead a recipient.
claims.quote: a subject heading of the message would be likely to mislead a recipient

claims.sentence: The message must be identified as an ad.
claims.quote: Identify the message as an ad.

claims.sentence: The statute calls for clear and conspicuous identification as an advertisement or solicitation.
claims.quote: clear and conspicuous identification that the message is an advertisement or solicitation

claims.sentence: The message must include a valid physical postal address.
claims.quote: Your message must include your valid physical postal address.

claims.sentence: The statute asks for a valid physical postal address of the sender.
claims.quote: a valid physical postal address of the sender

claims.sentence: Recipients must be told how to opt out.
claims.quote: Tell recipients how to opt out of receiving future marketing email from you.

claims.sentence: The statute asks for clear and conspicuous notice of the opportunity to decline.
claims.quote: clear and conspicuous notice of the opportunity under paragraph (3) to decline to receive further

claims.sentence: Opt-out requests must be honored within the stated number of business days.
claims.quote: You must honor a recipient’s opt-out request within 10 business days.

claims.sentence: A sender must monitor what others do on its behalf.
claims.quote: Monitor what others are doing on your behalf.

claims.sentence: An opt-out mechanism must process requests for at least 30 days after sending.
claims.quote: Any opt-out mechanism you offer must be able to process opt-out requests for at least 30 days after you send your message.

claims.sentence: The statute speaks of a functioning return address or Internet-based mechanism.
claims.quote: functioning return electronic mail address or other Internet-based mechanism

claims.sentence: After an opt-out a sender cannot sell or transfer the address.
claims.quote: you can’t sell or transfer their email addresses, even in the form of a mailing list.

claims.sentence: Hiring another company does not transfer legal responsibility.
claims.quote: even if you hire another company to handle your email marketing, you can’t contract away your legal responsibility

claims.sentence: The statute treats addresses generated by automated means as an aggravating factor.
claims.quote: obtained using an automated means that generates possible electronic mail addresses

claims.sentence: A seller paying or benefiting others for traffic or referrals is likely to have obligations.
claims.quote: the seller is likely to have compliance obligations under the CAN-SPAM Act.

claims.sentence: The guide states a per-email penalty figure.
claims.quote: Each separate email in violation of the CAN-SPAM Act is subject to penalties of up to $53,088

claims.sentence: Article 13(1) of the ePrivacy Directive refers to prior consent for direct marketing by electronic mail.
claims.quote: may only be allowed in respect of subscribers who have given their prior consent.

claims.sentence: The Government of Canada page refers to businesses obtaining consent before sending commercial electronic messages.
claims.quote: requesting amongst other things, that businesses obtain consent before sending commercial electronic messages.

claims.sentence: The federal provision says it is not unlawful for a person not acting under color of law to intercept a communication.
claims.quote: It shall not be unlawful under this chapter for a person not acting under color of law to intercept

claims.sentence: The provision applies where the person is a party to the communication.
claims.quote: a wire, oral, or electronic communication where such person is a party to the communication

claims.sentence: The provision applies where one party has given prior consent.
claims.quote: or where one of the parties to the communication has given prior consent to such interception

claims.sentence: The provision excludes interception for a criminal or tortious purpose.
claims.quote: unless such communication is intercepted for the purpose of committing any criminal or tortious act

claims.sentence: Stripe describes flat rate as customers choosing a service tier and paying a flat rate for it.
claims.quote: Customers choose a service tier (for example, Basic, Starter, or Enterprise) and pay a flat rate for it.

claims.sentence: Stripe describes per-seat pricing as one pricing unit per user.
claims.quote: Each pricing unit represents one user.

claims.sentence: Stripe describes tiered pricing as unit cost that changes with quantity or usage.
claims.quote: The unit cost changes with quantity (volume-based pricing) or usage (graduated pricing).

claims.sentence: Stripe describes usage-based pricing as charging by usage.
claims.quote: Charge customers based on their usage of your product or service.

claims.sentence: Microsoft Marketplace allows one of two pricing models per plan in a SaaS offer.
claims.quote: SaaS offers can use one of two pricing models with each plan

claims.sentence: All plans in the same Microsoft Marketplace offer must use the same pricing model.
claims.quote: All plans in the same offer must use the same pricing model.

claims.sentence: After publishing a Microsoft Marketplace offer the pricing model cannot be changed.
claims.quote: After you publish your offer, you can't change the pricing model.

claims.sentence: Stripe's trial offers documentation describes trials for items in a subscription.
claims.quote: Offer free or paid trials for items in a subscription.

claims.sentence: When a trial ends the subscription transitions to the regular or another configured price.
claims.quote: When the trial ends, the subscription automatically transitions to the regular price or another price you configure.

claims.sentence: One end-of-trial option for a missing payment method is to cancel.
claims.quote: Cancels the subscription.

claims.sentence: Another end-of-trial option for a missing payment method is to pause.
claims.quote: Pauses the subscription until you resume it.

claims.sentence: On the paused event a seller can revoke the customer's access.
claims.quote: you can revoke the customer’s access to the product

claims.sentence: Stripe suggests using the trial-ending event to send a reminder email.
claims.quote: Use this event to send your own reminder email.

claims.sentence: For one listing option the publisher manages the trial experience and the move to paid.
claims.quote: You manage the trial experience, including the transition to paid outside of the marketplace.

claims.sentence: Customers can cancel before a trial ends to avoid converting to paid.
claims.quote: Customers can cancel before the trial ends to avoid converting to a paid subscription.

claims.sentence: Section 8403 is headed Negative option marketing on the Internet.
claims.quote: Negative option marketing on the Internet

claims.sentence: The section opens with a prohibition on charging any consumer.
claims.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person to charge or attempt to charge any consumer for any goods or services

claims.sentence: The statute points to the FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule, 16 C.F.R. part 310, for the meaning of negative option feature.
claims.quote: negative option feature

claims.sentence: Condition one concerns disclosure of material terms.
claims.quote: provides text that clearly and conspicuously discloses all material terms of the transaction

claims.sentence: The disclosure is required before billing information is obtained.
claims.quote: obtaining the consumer's billing information

claims.sentence: Condition two concerns express informed consent before charging.
claims.quote: obtains a consumer's express informed consent before charging the consumer's credit card

claims.sentence: Condition three concerns simple mechanisms to stop recurring charges.
claims.quote: provides simple mechanisms for a consumer to stop recurring charges from being placed on the consumer's credit card

claims.sentence: Digital.gov states the first rule of plain language.
claims.quote: The first rule of plain language is: write for your audience.

claims.sentence: Digital.gov recommends the active voice.
claims.quote: Use the active voice. Active voice helps the message stay clear and easy-to-read.

claims.sentence: Digital.gov recommends lists.
claims.quote: Use lists. They can help you convey detailed information quickly without overloading your readers.

claims.sentence: The WAI tip on page titles.
claims.quote: For each web page, provide a short title that describes the page content and distinguishes it from other pages.

claims.sentence: The WAI tip on headings.
claims.quote: Use short headings to group related paragraphs and clearly describe the sections.

claims.sentence: The WAI tip on link text.
claims.quote: Write link text so that it describes the content of the link target.

claims.sentence: The WAI tip on image text alternatives.
claims.quote: For every image, write alternative text that provides the information or function of the image.

claims.sentence: The WAI tip on instructions and error messages.
claims.quote: Ensure that instructions, guidance, and error messages are clear, easy to understand, and avoid unnecessarily technical language.

claims.sentence: The WAI tip on clear and concise content.
claims.quote: Use simple language and formatting, as appropriate for the context.

claims.sentence: WCAG 2.4.2 requires titles that describe topic or purpose.
claims.quote: Web pages have titles that describe topic or purpose.

claims.sentence: The Understanding page explains why titles help in lists of results.
claims.quote: When titles appear in site maps or lists of search results, users can more quickly identify the content they need.

claims.sentence: WCAG 2.4.4 concerns link purpose determined from link text.
claims.quote: The purpose of each link can be determined from the link text alone

claims.sentence: WCAG 1.4.3 sets a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 for text.
claims.quote: The visual presentation of text and images of text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, except for the following:

claims.sentence: WCAG 1.4.3 sets a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 for large-scale text.
claims.quote: Large-scale text and images of large-scale text have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1;

claims.sentence: The FTC says the Guides do not have the force of law.
claims.quote: The Guides themselves don’t have the force of law.

claims.sentence: The FTC says practices inconsistent with the Guides may result in Section 5 actions.
claims.quote: practices inconsistent with the Guides may result in law enforcement actions alleging Section 5 violations.

claims.sentence: Section 465.2(a) addresses a business that would write, create or sell a consumer review.
claims.quote: for a business to write, create, or sell a consumer review

claims.sentence: Endorsements must reflect the endorser's honest opinions or experience.
claims.quote: Endorsements must reflect the honest opinions, findings, beliefs, or experience of the endorser.

claims.sentence: An endorsement may not be presented out of context or reworded to distort.
claims.quote: may not be presented out of context or reworded so as to distort

claims.sentence: Advertisers are subject to liability for misleading or unsubstantiated statements made through endorsements.
claims.quote: Advertisers are subject to liability for misleading or unsubstantiated statements made through endorsements.

claims.sentence: A consumer endorsement may be read as representing what consumers will generally achieve.
claims.quote: representative of what consumers will generally achieve

claims.sentence: Without substantiation the ad should disclose generally expected performance.
claims.quote: clearly and conspicuously disclose the generally expected performance in the depicted circumstances

claims.sentence: A connection between endorser and seller must be disclosed when it might affect weight or credibility.
claims.quote: When there exists a connection between the endorser and the seller of the advertised product

claims.sentence: The connection must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously.
claims.quote: such connection must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously

claims.sentence: The connection is one that might materially affect weight or credibility.
claims.quote: that might materially affect the weight or credibility of the endorsement

claims.sentence: Material connections can include a business, family or personal relationship.
claims.quote: Material connections can include a business, family, or personal relationship.

claims.sentence: Material connections can include monetary payment.
claims.quote: monetary payment

claims.sentence: The handbook defines a statistical test as a mechanism for quantitative decisions.
claims.quote: A statistical test provides a mechanism for making quantitative decisions about a process or processes.

claims.sentence: The handbook names the conjecture the null hypothesis.
claims.quote: The conjecture is called the null hypothesis.

claims.sentence: The alternative hypothesis may be what the tester believes true.
claims.quote: The alternative hypothesis might, in fact, be what we believe to be true.

claims.sentence: The test procedure keeps the risk of wrongly rejecting a true null hypothesis small; the page calls it the significance level.
claims.quote: The test procedure is constructed so that the risk of rejecting the null hypothesis, when it is in fact true, is small.

claims.sentence: The risk of missing a real difference is not chosen by the user.
claims.quote: The risk of failing to reject the null hypothesis when it is in fact false is not chosen by the user.

claims.sentence: A confidence interval gives a range of values likely to contain the parameter.
claims.quote: it provides a range of values which is likely to contain the population parameter of interest.

claims.sentence: Confidence intervals are built at a user-selected confidence level.
claims.quote: Confidence intervals are constructed at a confidence level, such as 95 %, selected by the user.

claims.sentence: The hypothesis of equal proportions can be tested with a z statistic.
claims.quote: The hypothesis of equal proportions can be tested using a z statistic

claims.sentence: The normal approximation applies when samples are reasonably large.
claims.quote: If the samples are reasonably large we can use the normal approximation to the binomial

claims.sentence: The Fisher Exact Probability test is suggested for small samples.
claims.quote: The Fisher Exact Probability test is an excellent choice for small samples
